decision: Accept Linux opt-in embedded mimalloc plus nonblocking completion readiness after final source-matched native/SDK tests. Default Rust library allocator choice remains with consumer; no storage backend change.
problem: CLI already uses mimalloc; embedded Rust allocations used System. Queue completion wakes callers before normal idle registration. Each standalone change had mixed latency/memory or response-shape effects.
design: Explicit embedded-mimalloc Cargo feature enables existing pinned allocator with local-dynamic TLS. Linux owner builds that feature; default rlib still admits a client allocator. Completion hint uses try_lock, skips busy queues, preserves FIFO, poison, input reservations and late reply ownership. Linux cdylib NODELETE keeps allocator callback/worker code mapped until process exit. Actual library allocator tag and CLI metadata attest compilation configuration in addition to source/artifact pins.
source_configuration_limit: Feature selection is not represented by source SHA alone. Artifact content pins, actual C ABI allocator tag, linked ELF flag, declared build features and preparation admission are retained.
resource_tradeoff: No pool/queue capacities or persistent user data change. Observed array-process RSS increases roughly 1.2–1.9 MiB for overlay and up to 0.9 MiB after materialization; SDK memory may increase a few MiB. MiMalloc reserves roughly 1 GiB additional virtual address space in this cohort, not 1 GiB resident RAM. Code mapping persists to process exit; Tofu version activation uses the existing process lifecycle, avoiding accumulating versions in one process. Scalar native driver lacks RSS columns and receives no scalar memory claim. These costs remain optimization targets.
causal_limit: Matched measurements support allocation/queue combination benefit, not exclusive causal attribution to worker migration or cache locality. Concurrent host work remains a variability limit. No universal all-scenario/all-metric SQLite claim.
defeated_alternatives: System-only allocation, process-wide preload, allocator alone, and completion hint alone. Preload alters host allocations; standalone measures do not establish broad replacement. All adverse rows retained.
